questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Statics of Particles and Force Systems
questions.text: State the Principle of Transmissibility of Forces and its limitations. State Varignon's Theorem of Moments and prove it algebraically and vectorially.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Friction, Wedges and Belt Friction
questions.text: State Coulomb's Laws of Dry Friction. Define Angle of Friction ($\phi = \tan^{-1}\mu$), Angle of Repose, and Cone of Friction. Prove that angle of repose is equal to the angle of limiting friction.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Friction, Wedges and Belt Friction
questions.text: Determine the minimum horizontal force $P$ required to be applied to a wedge of angle $15^\circ$ to raise a vertical block of weight $W = 5000\,\text{N}$. The coefficient of friction between all contact surfaces is $\mu = 0.25$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Friction, Wedges and Belt Friction
questions.text: Derive the Belt Friction equation for flat belts on a cylindrical pulley: $\frac{T_1}{T_2} = e^{\mu \theta}$ where $T_1, T_2$ are tight and slack side tensions and $\theta$ is the lap angle in radians. Modify the formula for V-belts ($\frac{T_1}{T_2} = e^{\mu \theta / \sin\beta}$).

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Centroids, Center of Gravity and Moment of Inertia
questions.text: Derive formulas for Centroid and Moment of Inertia of: (a) Triangular area of base $b$ and height $h$ about its base ($I = \frac{bh^3}{12}$) and centroidal axis ($I_G = \frac{bh^3}{36}$), and (b) Semicircular area of radius $R$ ($\bar{y} = \frac{4R}{3\pi}$).

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Centroids, Center of Gravity and Moment of Inertia
questions.text: State and prove Parallel Axis Theorem ($I_x = I_G + A d^2$) and Perpendicular Axis Theorem ($I_z = I_x + I_y$) for plane laminas. Calculate the principal centroidal moments of inertia $I_{xx}$ and $I_{yy}$ for an asymmetric T-section / I-section.

Explain Method of Joints and Method of Sections for analyzing determinate plane pin-jointed trusses. Determine the axial forces in members $CD, CL, ML$ of a Pratt bridge truss carrying vertical panel loads using the Method of Sections.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Statics of Particles and Force Systems
questions.text: What are Zero-Force Members in a truss? State inspection rules for identifying zero-force members. Draw Shear Force Diagram (SFD) and Bending Moment Diagram (BMD) for a simply supported beam with an overhang carrying a uniformly distributed load (UDL) and point loads, and locate the point of contraflexure.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Equilibrium of Rigid Bodies and Support Reactions
questions.text: State Newton's Second Law of Motion and D'Alembert's Dynamic Equilibrium Principle ($\sum \mathbf{F} - m\mathbf{a} = 0$). Solve for the acceleration and cable tension in a connected two-block system moving on an inclined plane.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Friction, Wedges and Belt Friction
questions.text: State the Principle of Work and Energy ($T_1 + U_{1-2} = T_2$) and Principle of Conservation of Mechanical Energy. A block of mass $m = 5\,\text{kg}$ slides down a curved frictionless track from height $h = 4\,\text{m}$ and compresses a linear spring of stiffness $k = 2000\,\text{N/m}$. Determine the maximum spring compression.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Equilibrium of Rigid Bodies and Support Reactions
questions.text: State Lami's Theorem for three coplanar concurrent forces in equilibrium. A sphere of weight $W = 1000\,\text{N}$ and radius $r = 20\,\text{cm}$ rests in a smooth V-shaped trough whose sides are inclined at $30^\circ$ and $60^\circ$ to the horizontal. Determine the normal reactions exerted by the sides on the sphere.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Statics of Particles and Force Systems
questions.text: Replace a given 3D force-couple system acting on a rigid body by an equivalent Single Wrench (Resultant force $\mathbf{R}$ and pitch $p$).

questions.chapter: Chapter 7: Kinetics of Particles and Rigid Bodies
questions.text: State the Principle of Impulse and Momentum ($\mathbf{I} = m\mathbf{v}_2 - m\mathbf{v}_1$). Define Coefficient of Restitution ($e = \frac{v_2 - v_1}{u_1 - u_2}$). Differentiate between Direct Central Impact and Oblique Central Impact of elastic spheres.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Statics of Particles and Force Systems
questions.text: A ladder of length $5\,\text{m}$ and weight $250\,\text{N}$ rests against a rough vertical wall and a rough horizontal floor with inclinations of $60^\circ$. A person of weight $750\,\text{N}$ climbs up the ladder. Find the maximum distance the person can climb before the ladder slips ($\mu_{floor} = 0.3, \mu_{wall} = 0.2$).
